newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sets aid package for leather firm.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sets aid package for leather firm.

text.p: The Australian government had finalised a financial support package for a leather producer at the centre of a trade dispute with the United States earlier this year, Industry Minister John Moore said on Friday.

The government would provide assistance to Melbourne-based Howe & Co Pty Ltd's capital investment programme, calculated as a maximum five percent of its projected sales over the period April 1997 to December 2000, Moore said in a statement.
The government would also help Howe with credit facilities over a longer period, he said.
"The package safeguards the jobs of around 500 employees and will ensure that Howe & Co can continue to invest and grow as planned," Moore said.

In October, Schaffer Corp Ltd, which holds 47.5 percent of Howe's owner, Australian Leather Holdings Ltd, said the U.S. government had instituted a Section 301 action under the U.S. Trade Act against Australian export incentives for the automotive leather upholstery industry.
But last month, Australia agreed to remove the industry from the incentive scheme after the U.S. agreed to drop a complaint to the World Trade Organisation.
The government agreed to compensate Howe, which had won a five-year contract to export A$25 million worth of leather to the U.S. for car seat covers, for future loss of income.
On Friday, Schaffer Corp said the arrangements should facilitate the satisfactory continuance of the business and enable Howe to continue a planned modernisation and capital investment programme.
